title: Jesus Pronounces Woes on the Scribes and Pharisees

questions.question: Jesus tells the crowds and His disciples that the scribes and the Pharisees sit on whose seat?
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:2 (ESV): "The scribes and the Pharisees sit on Moses' seat,"

questions.question: Jesus says to practice and observe whatever they tell you, but not to do what?
options: Not to do what they do, for they preach, but do not practice
Not to invite them to your homes
Not to listen to their prayers
questions.correctAnswer: Not to do what they do, for they preach, but do not practice
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:3 (ESV): "so do and observe whatever they tell you, but not the works they do. For they preach, but do not practice."

questions.question: The Pharisees do their deeds to be seen by others. They make their phylacteries broad and what else?
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:5 (ESV): "They do all their deeds to be seen by others. For they make their phylacteries broad and their fringes long,"

questions.question: Jesus commanded His followers not to be called by what three titles?
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:8-10 (ESV): "But you are not to be called rabbi... And call no man your father on earth... Neither be called instructors..."

questions.question: Jesus states a paradox of the kingdom: "The greatest among you shall be your..." what?
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:11 (ESV): "The greatest among you shall be your servant."

questions.question: What is the result for whoever exalts himself, and whoever humbles himself?
options: Whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted
Whoever exalts himself will rule, and whoever humbles himself will suffer
Both will finally be equal in the grave
Whoever exalts himself will gain wealth
questions.correctAnswer: Whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:12 (ESV): "Whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted."

questions.question: Jesus pronounces woe to the scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because they shut the kingdom of heaven in people's faces. What do they themselves do regarding the kingdom?
options: They neither enter themselves, nor allow those who would enter to go in
They steal the keys from others
They preach only to the Gentiles
questions.correctAnswer: They neither enter themselves, nor allow those who would enter to go in
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:13 (ESV): "...For you shut the kingdom of heaven in people's faces. For you neither enter yourselves nor allow those who would enter to go in."

questions.question: Jesus notes that they travel across sea and land to make a single proselyte, and when he becomes one, what do they make him?
options: Twice as much a child of hell as themselves
A wealthy merchant in the temple
questions.correctAnswer: Twice as much a child of hell as themselves
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:15 (ESV): "...and when he becomes a proselyte, you make him twice as much a child of hell as yourselves."

questions.question: Jesus calls them "blind guides" who strain out a gnat and swallow a what?
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:24 (ESV): "You blind guides, straining out a gnat and swallowing a camel!"

questions.question: Woe to them, for they tithe mint and dill and cumin, but they have neglected the weightier matters of the law. What are these weightier matters?
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:23 (ESV): "...and have neglected the weightier matters of the law: justice and mercy and faithfulness. These you ought to have done, without neglecting the others."

questions.question: Jesus compares the Pharisees to whitewashed tombs, which outwardly appear beautiful, but within are full of what?
options: Dead people's bones and all uncleanness
questions.correctAnswer: Dead people's bones and all uncleanness
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:27 (ESV): "...for you are like whitewashed tombs, which outwardly appear beautiful, but within are full of dead people's bones and all uncleanness."

questions.question: The Pharisees build the tombs of the prophets and say, "If we had lived in the days of our fathers, we would not have taken part with them in shedding the blood of the prophets." What does Jesus say they testify against themselves?
options: That they are sons of those who murdered the prophets
That they hated the prophets more
That they still want to kill Moses
That they are actually Romans in disguise
questions.correctAnswer: That they are sons of those who murdered the prophets
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:31 (ESV): "Thus you witness against yourselves that you are sons of those who murdered the prophets."

questions.question: How did Jesus frequently address the scribes and Pharisees during this chapter?
options: "Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites!"
questions.correctAnswer: "Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites!"
questions.explanation: Matthew 23 repeats "Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites!" seven times.

questions.question: Jesus laments over Jerusalem, saying, "O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, the city that kills the prophets." What did He desire to do for her children?
options: Gather her children together as a hen gathers her brood under her wings
Build a great wall of fire around them
Carry them across the sea to a new land
Rain down manna from heaven daily
questions.correctAnswer: Gather her children together as a hen gathers her brood under her wings
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:37 (ESV): "O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, the city that kills the prophets and stones those who are sent to it! How often would I have gathered your children together as a hen gathers her brood under her wings, and you were not willing!"

questions.question: Jesus tells Jerusalem that their house is left desolate, and they will not see Him again until they say what?
options: "Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord."
questions.correctAnswer: "Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord."
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:39 (ESV): "For I tell you, you will not see me again, until you say, 'Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.'"

key_verse_text: "Whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted."
